title: Slow-website latency hunt trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for slow-website-diagnosis trace events: one latency investigation — the budget split into levels of segments, the load and resource readings, the priced ceilings, and the stopwatch.

site.description: The site the complaint is about, e.g. shop.example.com.

journey.description: The page or user journey named in the complaint, e.g. 'the product page'.

complaint.description: The complaint as it was received, verbatim and unquantified.

stage.description: Technical lifecycle state of the hunt, translated by the visualizer; 'unchanged' means a fix was re-measured and moved nothing.

minutes.description: Minutes charged since the complaint landed; every action has a fixed deterministic cost.

budgetMs.description: The agreed 'fast enough' threshold in milliseconds; 0 while no budget has been set.

budgetLabel.description: What the budget applies to, e.g. 'the product page at p95'.

endToEndMs.description: The measured end-to-end total: the sum of the root level's segments, falling back to the read p95; 0 while nothing is measured.

percentiles.description: The shape of the latency distribution; absent until it is read.

avg.description: The mean, in ms — the number that describes nobody.

p50.description: The median, in ms — what a normal visit looks like.

p95.description: In ms — what the person complaining is living through.

p99.description: In ms — the shape of the tail.

levels.description: The splits, outermost first. The root level is named 'end-to-end'; every later level is named after the segment that was drilled into.

name.description: 'end-to-end' for the root, otherwise the parent segment's name.

totalMs.description: The sum of this level's segments; it should equal the parent segment it splits.

segments.description: The measured slices of this level, in the order they were measured.

name.description: What was measured, e.g. 'waiting for the first byte (TTFB)'.

tool.description: What produced the number, e.g. 'the browser network panel' or 'EXPLAIN ANALYZE'.

status.description: 'hotspot' is the biggest slice not yet cleared; 'drilled' means it was opened into its own level.

note.description: The evidence that cleared the segment; empty otherwise.

hotspot.description: The biggest uncleared segment of the deepest level, or null before anything is measured.

facts.description: The questions that turned the complaint into a request, in order.

question.description: The question put to whoever complained.

answer.description: The answer that narrowed the hunt.

load.description: The same request timed with the site idle and at peak; absent until compared.

idleMs.description: Milliseconds with nobody on the site — the work itself.

peakMs.description: Milliseconds at peak — the work plus the wait.

queueing.description: True when peak is at least twice idle: most of the latency is a queue, not work.

resources.description: Resource readings taken while looking for a queue, in the order they were read.

name.description: The resource, e.g. 'the JDBC connection pool'.

reading.description: The reading itself, including anything waiting in line.

saturated.description: Whether requests are queueing for it.

ceilings.description: Proposed optimisations priced against the whole request (Amdahl's law), in the order they were priced.

speedup.description: How many times faster that segment would become.

savedMs.description: Milliseconds it can remove — its ceiling.

gainPercent.description: Those milliseconds as a percentage of the end-to-end total.

worthIt.description: Whether the gain clears the 10% noise floor.

missingSignals.description: Measurements that do not exist, which is why the hunt is guesswork.

cause.description: The confirmed cause, or null while nothing accounts for the time.

causeEvidence.description: The measurement that made the cause more than a story.

fix.description: The change that was shipped; absent while nothing has been changed.

expectedMs.description: The milliseconds it was expected to remove, written down before the deploy.

blind.description: True when it shipped with no confirmed cause.

result.description: The same measurement taken again; absent until it is.

beforeMs.description: The end-to-end total before the change.

improved.description: False when the gain is under the 10% noise floor.

metBudget.description: Whether the new number is inside the agreed budget.

guards.description: The monitoring left behind so the next hunt starts from data.

missteps.description: Hunting errors recorded as consequences of the order actions were taken in.
